Remuneration Committee Remit                                                                                                                        How the Committee addresses the requirements under Provision 40 in the Code
The role of the Committee is to recommend to the Board a strategy and framework for remuneration for Executive Directors and senior
                                                                                                                                                    Principle                    Committee approach
management which will attract and retain leaders who are focused and incentivised to deliver the Company’s strategic business priorities
within a framework which is aligned with the interests of our shareholders and designed to promote the long term success of the Company.            Clarity                      – We have operated a consistent approach which is well reported in our Directors’ Remuneration Reports.
It is also responsible for reviewing wider workforce remuneration practices and policies.                                                                                          Our approach is understood internally by employees and externally with strong levels of shareholder support
Details of Committee membership and attendance at meetings can be found on page 105.
                                                                                                                                                    Simplicity                   – Executive Director remuneration arrangements have been designed, in accordance with best practice,
The Committee reviewed its Terms of Reference in 2021 and evaluated its own performance against them. Following this review, the                                                   to be as simple as possible
Committee confirmed that they remain appropriate. The Terms of Reference can be found on the Company’s corporate website.
No Director is involved in any decisions about their own remuneration and a conflicts of interest register is maintained by the Company             Risk                         – We mitigate risk through careful plan design, including long term performance measurement, deferral, and
Secretary in accordance with the Company’s Conflicts of Interest Policy.                                                                                                           shareholding requirements (including post cessation of employment) and discretion and clawback provisions

The Group’s activities expose it to the financial risks of changes in both foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. The Group aims to
manage the exposure to these risks using fixed or variable rate borrowings, foreign currency borrowings and derivative financial instruments.                Credit risk
(a) Interest rate risk management                                                                                                                            Credit risk is the risk of financial loss where counterparties are not able to meet their obligations.

provided by the fund managers and collated by Northern Trust as custodian, who independently price the securities from their preferred
vendor sources where the data is publicly available and rely on investment manager data where this information is not available. Where
available, the fair values are quoted prices (e.g. listed equity). Unlisted investments (e.g. private equity) are included at values provided by
the fund manager in accordance with relevant guidance. Other significant assets are valued based on observable inputs.
There are no investments in respect of the Group’s own securities.

in order to assess the underlying operational performance of the Group and, as such, these measures should be considered alongside IFRS                  Adjusted basic and diluted earnings per share
